# Definition of Done

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

Applies to every project; project additions are `DoD-Pnn` in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`.
Each item needs evidence in `docs/06_verification-report.md`.

| ID | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| DoD-01 | The full test suite passes; frozen test hashes match the manifest | test report, hash check |
| DoD-02 | Format, lint, type check and static analysis report no errors | tool output |
| DoD-03 | The quality gate of `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` ("Quality gate") is met for each component, or the shortfall after the third survivor round is recorded with a decision | coverage and mutation reports with scope, raw and adjusted score, rounds |
| DoD-04 | Architecture constraints (`AR`) are checked automatically where possible; no dependency cycles | architecture test output |
| DoD-05 | No open Critical or High finding from the security review and scanners | `general/skills/verify-release` output |
| DoD-06 | Every component runs in its target environment and the core user flows work at runtime, not only in tests | runtime demonstration log |
| DoD-07 | Every AC traces to at least one test and one commit | traceability table |
| DoD-08 | Root and component READMEs (ES-06) work when followed from a clean checkout | clone log |
| DoD-09 | Release notes list everything a human must test manually | `docs/release-notes.md` |
| DoD-10 | Every decision has a resolution or is listed as pending review; inputs and protected files are unchanged | decisions log, `docs/00_input-manifest.sha256` check |
| DoD-11 | The evidence checks in `general/phases.md` hold | `general/phases.md`, "Evidence" |
# Measurement scope

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 3, 5, 6 · Agent: read-only

Defines what test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size mean, so that figures from different runs compare. Record every figure in `run-log.json` → `codeMetrics` and in `docs/06_verification-report.md` with its scope, level and tool. The project selects paths and exclusions in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Mutation scope"); this file never names them.

## Constraints

- Do not change a tool's scope, filters, exclusions or thresholds to improve a number. A change is a decision record.
- Do not report a figure without its scope, level and tool.
- Production code is the source a component ships. It excludes tests, generated code, the application entry point and anything listed under "Measurement exclusions" in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with a reason. Decide the exclusions in phase 3, before any test is written; do not extend them later.
- Test code never counts towards coverage or mutation.

## Test counts

Per component and level (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e`), passed and failed, from the runner's own report.

## Coverage

Line and branch, per component, as three figures: `unit` (unit tests only), `nonUnit` (integration, acceptance and end-to-end tests that exercise the component) and `all` (one merged report). The headline figure is `all`.

## Mutation score

- **Scope:** all production code of the component, narrowed only to the paths in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` "Mutation scope", which are the same in every run of the project (default: all production code). Do not narrow it by running only some tests or by excluding packages that are not listed there.
- **Tests:** the component's full automated suite, at every level it has, so the score does not depend on which level the agent ran. If that is infeasible, record the tests actually run and the reason in a decision record.
- **Record:** `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`. `score` (raw) = killed (timed-out counts as killed) ÷ all mutants the tool generated; a mutant no test reaches counts as survived. `scoreAdjusted` = (killed + equivalent) ÷ total, where `equivalent` is the number of survivors justified as equivalent. `scoreCovered` = killed ÷ mutants a test reaches.
- Do not remove equivalent mutants by hand. List every survivor you count as equivalent in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with the class and method, the mutation and the reason it cannot change behaviour; a survivor without that entry is not equivalent. Always record the raw score next to the adjusted score.

## Code size

`cloc` (same version in every run): production = non-test source and resources, test = test sources including end-to-end tests. Generated code and lock files are excluded.

## Mutation run discipline

- Measure coverage and mutation score in phase 5, so that surviving mutants are handled before verification. Phase 6 repeats a measurement only for a component whose code or tests changed since, and only once, after the last fix.
- Do not start a full mutation run on code that is not final. One full run per component per measurement; the only other runs are the targeted survivor rounds and the one confirming full run after the last round of the quality gate (below).
- Check once, before the full run, that the tool works: a mutant in code the tests plainly cover must be killed. A score far below the line coverage (for example 25 % at 100 % coverage) means the tool is not activating mutants (known case: Stryker with the wrong Vitest major version); stop and raise a decision, do not record the figure.
- Start a long run in the background and continue with other checks of the phase; read its log only for the summary lines. Do not hold the session in a blocking wait on it.

## Quality gate

The gate is the same in every run of the project: the thresholds in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Thresholds"), per component, over the scope and with the tests defined above. It makes runs comparable: every run reaches the same quality, and what differs is the cost of reaching it.

- **Gate:** line coverage (`all`) at or above the line threshold, and `scoreAdjusted` at or above the mutation threshold. Branch coverage is recorded only.
- **Order in phase 5:** write the unit and integration tests area by area and measure line coverage after each area (fast) until the line threshold is met; then run mutation testing **once** per component (full run); then, if `scoreAdjusted` is below the threshold, up to **three** survivor rounds: each adds tests aimed at the survivors in the code that matters most (validation, security, persistence, business rules first) and re-runs only the mutated classes, with one confirming full run after the last round.
- **Stop at the gate:** once a component meets both thresholds, add no further test and start no further mutation run for it. Do not add tests for coverage or score beyond the gate.
- **Shortfall:** after the third round a component still below a threshold is recorded as a shortfall (which threshold, by how many points) in a non-blocking decision and as a finding, and the run continues. Do not change the scope, the tests run or the exclusions to reach a threshold; that is a decision record at most.
- **Record in `run-log.json`:** `codeMetrics.gate` = `{ thresholds: {lineCoverage, mutationScore}, perComponent: { <name>: { lineMet, mutationMet, lineShortfall, mutationShortfall } }, mutationRounds: { <name>: n }, testsAtFirstMutation: { <name>: n }, met: true|false }`; `mutationRounds` is 0 when the first full run already met the gate.
# Severity scale

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 0, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

The only levels used anywhere. Critical and High block release.

| Level | Definition | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Exploitable now, or total loss of a core user story with no workaround | Unauthenticated access to protected data; accepted input that is silently not stored |
| High | Exploitable under realistic conditions, or a core user story degraded for a plausible group of users | Missing authorization check on one operation; a limit that locks out legitimate users |
| Medium | A real defect with limited impact, or a control weaker than required | A dependency vulnerability with no reachable exploit path; a duplicated validation rule |
| Low | Cosmetic, stylistic, or a theoretical or false-positive finding | A lint warning; a scanner match on constant input |

## Rules

- Tools that report Critical/High/Medium/Low (or CVSS) are used as reported.
- Lowering a Critical or High to Medium or Low needs written evidence (e.g. the vulnerable feature is not used) and is a blocking decision.
- A surviving mutant in security-, validation- or persistence-related code is classified individually.

## Tool mapping

Extend when a project adds a tool with its own scale.

| Tool type | Tool's level | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| CVSS-based (dependency scanners) | 9.0–10.0 / 7.0–8.9 / 4.0–6.9 / 0.1–3.9 | Critical / High / Medium / Low |
| Rule-based SAST with ERROR/WARNING/INFO | ERROR / WARNING / INFO | High / Medium / Low |
| Rank or priority 1–5 scales | 1 / 2 / 3–5 | High / Medium / Low |
| Bug-rank 1–20 scales | 1–4 / 5–9 / 10–20 | High / Medium / Low |
# Test strategy

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: every phase that writes or runs tests · Agent: read-only

When each test level is written and whether it is frozen is defined in `general/phases.md`. Project thresholds are in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`.

## Constraints

- Do not test acceptance behaviour through internals; use the component's public interface (API, UI, CLI, messages).
- Do not depend on live external services in automated tests; use the local substitutes in `project/00_setup/environments.md` and list the real services in the release notes for manual testing.
- Do not leave flaky, skipped or disabled tests; fix them or record a decision.
- Do not weaken an assertion to make an incorrect implementation pass.
- Test names contain the AC id they verify.

## First complete run

Record the result of the first full run before fixing anything, then classify each failure:

| Class | Action |
|---|---|
| Implementation defect | fix the code |
| Defect in a non-frozen test | fix the test and say so in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` |
| Frozen test appears wrong | blocking decision; do not touch the test |

## Measures (recorded in every project)

Test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: what each covers, at which level and with which tool.

## Manifest

`docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256` uses `sha256sum` format with paths relative to `02_output/`, hashed after LF normalisation.
# Security baseline

> Owner: Security officer · Read in: phases 0, 2, 6 · Agent: read-only

Applies to every project. Project requirements (`SR-nn`) and the chosen standard level are in `project/02_design/security-requirements.md`.

## Verification standard by component type

| Component type | Standard | Default level |
|---|---|---|
| Web app, API, service | OWASP ASVS (latest) | Level 1; Level 2 when handling authentication, payments or sensitive personal data |
| Mobile app | OWASP MASVS (latest) | L1 |
| Desktop app, CLI, library | Applicable OWASP ASVS chapters | Level 1 |

## Controls for every project

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SB-01 | All input is validated on the trusted side (server or core), whatever the client does. |
| SB-02 | Every non-public operation checks authentication and authorization. |
| SB-03 | Credentials are stored only as salted, slow hashes; secrets come from configuration (ES-01, ES-02). |
| SB-04 | Data in transit uses TLS outside the local machine. |
| SB-05 | Output is encoded for its context; queries are parameterised. |
| SB-06 | Public and authentication endpoints are rate limited. |
| SB-07 | Errors and logs expose no internals, secrets or personal data (ES-07). |
| SB-08 | Dependencies are scanned; no known Critical or High vulnerability ships. |
| SB-09 | Source is scanned with static analysis and a secret scanner. |
| SB-10 | Web responses carry security headers (content security policy, framing, content-type options). |
| SB-11 | Deployed processes run with least privilege (e.g. non-root containers). |

## Personal data (privacy)

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SB-12 | Collect only the personal data a requirement needs; the project lists it. |
| SB-13 | Each personal-data item has a stated purpose and retention period. |
| SB-14 | Consent, where required, is explicit and never preselected. |

# Measurement scope

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 3, 5, 6 · Agent: read-only

Defines what test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size mean, so that figures from different runs compare. Record every figure in `run-log.json` → `codeMetrics` and in `docs/06_verification-report.md` with its scope, level and tool. The project selects paths and exclusions in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Mutation scope"); this file never names them.

## Constraints

- Do not change a tool's scope, filters, exclusions or thresholds to improve a number. A change is a decision record.
- Do not report a figure without its scope, level and tool.
- Production code is the source a component ships. It excludes tests, generated code, the application entry point and anything listed under "Measurement exclusions" in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with a reason. Decide the exclusions in phase 3, before any test is written; do not extend them later.
- Test code never counts towards coverage or mutation.

## Test counts

Per component and level (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e`), passed and failed, from the runner's own report.

## Coverage

Line and branch, per component, as three figures: `unit` (unit tests only), `nonUnit` (integration, acceptance and end-to-end tests that exercise the component) and `all` (one merged report). The headline figure is `all`.

## Mutation score

- **Scope:** all production code of the component, narrowed only to the paths in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` "Mutation scope", which are the same in every run of the project (default: all production code). Do not narrow it by running only some tests or by excluding packages that are not listed there.
- **Tests:** the component's full automated suite, at every level it has, so the score does not depend on which level the agent ran. If that is infeasible, record the tests actually run and the reason in a decision record.
- **Record:** `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`. `score` (raw) = killed (timed-out counts as killed) ÷ all mutants the tool generated; a mutant no test reaches counts as survived. `scoreAdjusted` = (killed + equivalent) ÷ total, where `equivalent` is the number of survivors justified as equivalent. `scoreCovered` = killed ÷ mutants a test reaches.
- Do not remove equivalent mutants by hand. List every survivor you count as equivalent in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with the class and method, the mutation and the reason it cannot change behaviour; a survivor without that entry is not equivalent. Always record the raw score next to the adjusted score.

## Code size

`cloc` (same version in every run): production = non-test source and resources, test = test sources including end-to-end tests. Generated code and lock files are excluded.

## Mutation run discipline

- Measure coverage and mutation score in phase 5, so that surviving mutants are handled before verification. Phase 6 repeats a measurement only for a component whose code or tests changed since, and only once, after the last fix.
- Do not start a full mutation run on code that is not final. One full run per component per measurement; the only other runs are the targeted survivor rounds and the one confirming full run after the last round of the quality gate (below).
- Check once, before the full run, that the tool works: a mutant in code the tests plainly cover must be killed. A score far below the line coverage (for example 25 % at 100 % coverage) means the tool is not activating mutants (known case: Stryker with the wrong Vitest major version); stop and raise a decision, do not record the figure.
- Start a long run in the background and continue with other checks of the phase; read its log only for the summary lines. Do not hold the session in a blocking wait on it.

## Quality gate

The gate is the same in every run of the project: the thresholds in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Thresholds"), per component, over the scope and with the tests defined above. It makes runs comparable: every run reaches the same quality, and what differs is the cost of reaching it.

- **Gate:** line coverage (`all`) at or above the line threshold, and `scoreAdjusted` at or above the mutation threshold. Branch coverage is recorded only.
- **Order in phase 5:** write the unit and integration tests area by area and measure line coverage after each area (fast) until the line threshold is met; then run mutation testing **once** per component (full run); then, if `scoreAdjusted` is below the threshold, up to **three** survivor rounds: each adds tests aimed at the survivors in the code that matters most (validation, security, persistence, business rules first) and re-runs only the mutated classes, with one confirming full run after the last round.
- **Stop at the gate:** once a component meets both thresholds, add no further test and start no further mutation run for it. Do not add tests for coverage or score beyond the gate.
- **Shortfall:** after the third round a component still below a threshold is recorded as a shortfall (which threshold, by how many points) in a non-blocking decision and as a finding, and the run continues. Do not change the scope, the tests run or the exclusions to reach a threshold; that is a decision record at most.
- **Record in `run-log.json`:** `codeMetrics.gate` = `{ thresholds: {lineCoverage, mutationScore}, perComponent: { <name>: { lineMet, mutationMet, lineShortfall, mutationShortfall } }, mutationRounds: { <name>: n }, testsAtFirstMutation: { <name>: n }, met: true|false }`; `mutationRounds` is 0 when the first full run already met the gate.

# Acceptance criteria

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 3, 6 · Agent: read-only

This list is an input, the same in every run of this project: the agent does not derive, add, merge or reword criteria. Each criterion states one observable behaviour (Given / When / Then) and cites its story and rules. "Rejected" always means: the API answers with an error status and field errors, no database row and no JSON copy are created, and no email is sent. The open questions are answered in `scope.md` (OQ-01 to OQ-06).

Common terms used below:

- *valid external submission*: registration type `EXTERNAL`; first name, last name, email, organization filled; every mandatory consent given; a reCAPTCHA token the verifier accepts; zero or more distinct active option ids available to the type.
- *valid student submission*: as above with type `STUDENT` and study institution, study programme and student ID instead of organization.

## US-001 External participant registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-001-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid external submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-001-02 | Given the external form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, organization) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-001-03 | Given a valid external submission whose text fields have leading and trailing spaces, when it is accepted, then the stored values have the spaces removed. | BR-02 |
| AC-001-04 | Given the external form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-001-05 | Given the external form, when an option id is unknown, inactive or listed twice, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, SR-04, OQ-04 |
| AC-001-06 | Given the external form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, OQ-02 |
| AC-001-07 | Given the external form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01, scope (anti-automation) |
| AC-001-08 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "external participant", then the page shows exactly the external fields, the active options grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities, and every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05 |

## US-002 Student registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-002-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid student submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-002-02 | Given the student form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-002-03 | Given the student form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-002-04 | Given an active option configured as not available to students, when a student submission selects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, OQ-01 |
| AC-002-05 | Given the student form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, OQ-02 |
| AC-002-06 | Given the student form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01 |
| AC-002-07 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "student", then the page shows exactly the student fields and only the active options available to students, grouped by category, with every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05, OQ-01 |

## US-003 Configurable conference options

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-003-01 | Given a configuration with active and inactive options, when the form configuration is requested, then it lists only the active options, each with its identifier, display name, category and the registration types it is available to. | BR-04 |
| AC-003-02 | Given the backend is started with a different options configuration (an option added, one deactivated), when the form configuration is requested, then it reflects the new configuration, with no code change. | AR-04 |
| AC-003-03 | Given an options configuration that is invalid (duplicate identifier, unknown category, missing name), when the backend starts, then it refuses to start. | AR-04 |

## US-004 Registration confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Format

## Stories

Epic: as a conference organizer, I want participants to register online, so that registrations are collected and managed reliably.

### US-001 External participant registration

As an external participant, I want to register using the external participant form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities I select.
In scope: the external form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: payment, accounts, editing a submitted registration.

### US-002 Student registration

As a student, I want to register using the student form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities available to students.
In scope: the student form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: verifying student status externally, accounts.

### US-003 Configurable conference options

As an organizer, I want workshops, events, meals and other optional activities to be configurable, so that the system can be reused when the programme changes.
Out of scope: an administration UI for options.

### US-004 Registration confirmation

As a participant, I want a clear confirmation in the application after my registration is processed, so that I know it was received (BR-06).

### US-005 Reliable registration storage

As an organizer, I want every accepted registration stored reliably, so that none is lost and each can be recovered (BR-07).

### US-006 Participant email confirmation

As a participant, I want an email confirming my registration, so that I have a record of it.

### US-007 Organizer notification

As an organizer, I want an email when someone registers, containing the submitted data with the raw registration JSON attached, so that I can monitor incoming registrations.

### US-008 Registration export

As an organizer, I want to export the current registrations as an Excel workbook, so that I can process them outside the system (BR-08).

## Authentication and authorization

- Participants are anonymous; there are no participant accounts.
- One organizer role may export registrations (BR-08). The mechanism is decided in phase 2, using the organizer credentials from `secrets.env.example`; identity providers are out of scope.
- Everything else (options, registration) is public but protected by SR-01 and SR-03.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SR-01 | Every registration is protected by Google reCAPTCHA v2 and verified on the backend; the frontend check alone is never enough. |
| SR-02 | reCAPTCHA test mode is enabled only by environment configuration, never by default; production refuses to start with test mode on or with empty keys. |
| SR-03 | Every public `/api` endpoint (form configuration, registration, export) is rate limited per client, and request bodies have a size limit. |
| SR-04 | Option identifiers are checked against the active configured set (BR-04). |
| SR-05 | Email content is generated safely: user input cannot inject headers or markup. |
| SR-06 | Organizer credentials are never accepted over plain HTTP, except on localhost. |
| SR-07 | The export and the organizer email expose only registration data, never internal fields or other system data. |
| SR-08 | The reverse proxy in front of the backend never forwards a client-supplied `Host` header; it sets the upstream host itself. |

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Stories

Epic: as a conference organizer, I want participants to register online, so that registrations are collected and managed reliably.

### US-001 External participant registration

As an external participant, I want to register using the external participant form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities I select.
In scope: the external form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: payment, accounts, editing a submitted registration.

### US-002 Student registration

As a student, I want to register using the student form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities available to students.
In scope: the student form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: verifying student status externally, accounts.

### US-003 Configurable conference options

As an organizer, I want workshops, events, meals and other optional activities to be configurable, so that the system can be reused when the programme changes.
Out of scope: an administration UI for options.

### US-004 Registration confirmation

As a participant, I want a clear confirmation in the application after my registration is processed, so that I know it was received (BR-06).

### US-005 Reliable registration storage

As an organizer, I want every accepted registration stored reliably, so that none is lost and each can be recovered (BR-07).

### US-006 Participant email confirmation

As a participant, I want an email confirming my registration, so that I have a record of it.

### US-007 Organizer notification

As an organizer, I want an email when someone registers, containing the submitted data with the raw registration JSON attached, so that I can monitor incoming registrations.

### US-008 Registration export

As an organizer, I want to export the current registrations as an Excel workbook, so that I can process them outside the system (BR-08).

| SR-06 | Organizer credentials are never accepted over plain HTTP, except on localhost. |

1. In the **finished session**, before you close it, copy these numbers from the **Usage panel** (the harness's own figures) into the empty cells of the panel table in `03_statistics/usage.md`: *Cost shown*, *API time*, *Session wall time*, *Tokens shown per model* (input, output, cache read, cache write), *Share of usage at over 150k context* and *Plan limits used*. The transcript of a local session does not always contain these numbers, and without them the cost is not cross-checked. If you type `/cost` and it works, the tool reads the numbers from the transcript and you can skip this.
2. Open a **new session in the same folder** and send exactly:

   ```
   Run node 03_statistics/tools/build-report.mjs --run 03_statistics and report what it prints. Do not change anything else.
   ```

3. Add the number of **approval prompts** to `03_statistics/usage.md` (the only cell it cannot fill).

# Metrics

> Owner: Experiment lead · Read in: every phase and post-run · Agent: read-only

Experiment measurement only. Record observed values; never estimate. An unobservable value stays `null` with a `<field>Reason`.

Goal column: **↓** lower is better, **↑** higher is better, **=** should equal the stated value, **i** information for interpreting other numbers.

## Principles

- **Human waiting is not part of the result.** Agent time is wall time minus every wait for a human. A wait over one hour also lets the 1-hour prompt cache expire, and the call after it writes the whole context again; that rebuild is a cost of the wait, so `usage.costUsdExclWaits` removes it. Compare runs on agent time and `costUsdExclWaits`.
- **Record only what only you can see, and with the clock tool.** The agent records what happened (waits, loops, decisions, deviations, test and quality results). Timestamps come from `tools/stat.mjs`, never from memory or estimates. Everything that can be computed from the transcripts and git is computed after the run by `tools/build-report.mjs`, so the run spends no calls on it.
- **Make runs comparable.** Say what a number covers. Scope, level and tool of coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

Phase 0, first action: `node 03_statistics/tools/stat.mjs init`. It creates `run-log.json` from the template, a unique `runId`, the start time and commit, the transcript path and the environment. It prints what it wrote.

100	## Principles
101	
102	- **Human waiting is not part of the result.** Agent time is wall time minus every wait for a human. A wait over one hour also lets the 1-hour prompt cache expire, and the call after it writes the whole context again; that rebuild is a cost of the wait, so `usage.costUsdExclWaits` removes it. Compare runs on agent time and `costUsdExclWaits`.
103	- **Record only what only you can see, and with the clock tool.** The agent records what happened (waits, loops, decisions, deviations, test and quality results). Timestamps come from `tools/stat.mjs`, never from memory or estimates. Everything that can be computed from the transcripts and git is computed after the run by `tools/build-report.mjs`, so the run spends no calls on it.
104	- **Make runs comparable.** Say what a number covers. Scope, level and tool of coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

127	## 2. Post-run session → `run-log.json`, `results/`, `data/`
128	
129	Started after the run ends, in a new session whose only task is: "Run `node 03_statistics/tools/build-report.mjs --run 03_statistics` and report what it prints. Do not change anything else." Before it, run `/cost` once in the finished session (the plan limits are then captured in the transcript). The script:
130	
131	1. measures the run from the session transcript(s), the sub-agent transcripts next to them and `git log`, and stores `time`, `usage`, `environment`, `commits`, `commitSummary` in `run-log.json`;
132	2. copies the transcripts to `03_statistics/data/` (committed with the run, so the measuring can be repeated on any machine; the recorded path is used when it exists, the copy otherwise);
133	3. writes everything it generates to `03_statistics/results/`: `run-report.html` (every attribute with goal, direction and value), `measurements.json`, `usage-panel.md`, `commits.csv`, `transcript.md` (readable session, needs Python 3);
134	4. fills the empty cells of the panel table in `usage.md` from the harness's own accounting (the `cost-state` record in the transcript).

136	Options: `--no-write` leaves `run-log.json` and `usage.md` alone, `--no-md` skips `transcript.md`, `--no-backup` skips `data/`. # Run guide

This setup is run three times, once each by kyuhi, tanej and tjan, in one shared environment, and the three runs are compared. Everything below is therefore the same for everyone; the only things that may differ are the four lines in the table "If you are not kyuhi".

## 1. Prepare the run folder
1. **Copy the template** (the folder `kyuhi_single-agent_sdd_v005_structure`) to a new folder named after the run, for example `kyuhi_single-agent_sdd_v005`. Open a terminal in it.
2. **Initialise git on the run's branch and keep `.env` out of git before you create it.** The branch is named `<operator>/single-agent/sdd/v005` (for kyuhi: `kyuhi/single-agent/sdd/v005`).
   - `git init -b kyuhi/single-agent/sdd/v005` (use your own operator name)
   - then exclude `.env` (the template has no `.gitignore`; the agent writes one in phase 0):
   - Git Bash: `echo .env >> .git/info/exclude`
   - PowerShell: `Add-Content -Encoding ascii .git\info\exclude ".env"`
3. **Copy the project inputs** `01_input/01_project/` and paste it into run directory.
4. **Check `01_input/01_project/00_setup/run-config.md`.**
      - operator `kyuhi`, 
      - machine `kyuhiPC`, 
      - plan `PRO`, 
      - permission mode `auto`, 
      - model `claude-opus-5-5`, 
      - effort `medium`
      - Run label: **change it for every run** (`kyuhi_single-agent_sdd_v005`, then `v006`,...).
      - Run ID: **keep empty it generates by itself**
      - Starting commit: **keep empty it generates by itself**
5. **Check the price row in `03_statistics/usage.md`.** It is pre-filled for Opus 5.5; change it only if the prices or the model changed.
6. **Create `.env`**: copy `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` to `.env` in the run folder and fill every value (database password, organizer login, NVD key). Never paste a secret into the chat.
7. **Commit the inputs**: `git add -A`, `git commit -m "initial commit"`. Check that `git status` does not list `.env` (it must be clean) before anything is pushed.
8. **Connect to the shared runs repository and push the initial setup** (so the start state is on record before the agent starts):
   ```bash
   git remote add origin https://github.com/SQA-interns/Structured_Input_Files.git
   git push -u origin kyuhi/single-agent/sdd/v005
   ```
   Use your own operator name in the branch. Every operator pushes to a branch of its own in this repository, never to `main`. Sign in to GitHub when asked. If `git remote add` says the remote already exists, check it with `git remote -v` and fix it with `git remote set-url origin https://github.com/SQA-interns/Structured_Input_Files.git`. Do not push before `.env` is confirmed absent from `git status`.
9. **Set the same permission mode** you set in `run-config.md`.
10. **Check the environment** (the same for all three operators): Docker Engine 29.8.1 and Compose 5.5.1, Node 24.13.0, Java 21, internet access for the scanners (NVD key in `.env`), no other heavy load on the machine during the run, one session only.

**If you are not kyuhi**, change only these lines in `01_input/01_project/00_setup/run-config.md` and nothing else (not the inputs, not the tools):

| Line | kyuhi | tanej | tjan |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operator | `kyuhi` | `tanej` | `tjan` |
| Machine | `kyuhiPC` | a label of your computer | a label of your computer |
| Plan | `PRO` | your plan | your plan |
| Run label | `kyuhi_single-agent_sdd_v005` | `tanej_single-agent_sdd_v005` | `tjan_single-agent_sdd_v005` |

## 2. Start the run
Open a **new agent session in the run folder** (only one session per run; do not open other sessions in this folder, the newest one is taken as the run's transcript) and send exactly:

```
Read AGENTS.md and start.
```

## 3. During the run
- Answer tooling and environment questions with the standard answers below, the same way in every run.
- The acceptance criteria, the end-to-end scenarios and the answers to the open questions are inputs, so the agent should not ask about business behaviour. If it does anyway, answer only: *"No further information is available. Choose the proposed default option and record it as a decision."*
- To **any other question not listed below**, give the same answer in every run: *"Choose the proposed default option and record it as a decision."* A frozen acceptance test that cannot pass (a defect in the test harness or in one assertion): approve the agent's proposed default fix (option 1). Do not add your own ideas or hints; different answers make the runs incomparable.
- The agent works until the **quality gate** is met (mutation score 90 %, line coverage 95 %, per component). Do not tell it to stop earlier or to go further.
- Type at least one line of each answer yourself; a pasted-only answer makes the agent ask you to confirm.
- Do not change the input files. Do not leave a question unanswered for more than an hour: the cache expires and the wait is excluded from the results, but the time is lost. If you must stop, tell the agent so it records the wait.

**Standard answers (conference registration project; decision numbers differ, recognise them by subject)**
| Phase | The agent asks about | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Host JDK, Node, npm or Docker differs from the pins by a patch version | No question: pre-approved (PA-05). Anything else (a different minor or major version): approve the installed version only if the agent says everything runs. |
| 0 | `vitest` or `jscpd` has Critical or High vulnerabilities | Move to the fixed versions the agent proposes (`jscpd` 5.4.0). `vitest` and `@vitest/coverage-v8` stay on 4.1.11: 5.x does not work with Stryker (see phase 6). No question if `tech-stack.md` already has them. |
| 0 | CVE-2025-7962 on `angus-activation`, CVE-2025-15104 on `hibernate-validator`, dev-only `npm audit` advisories | No question: pre-approved in `01_project/00_setup/pre-approved.md` (PA-01 to PA-03). If the agent asks anyway, answer: *use pre-approved.md*. |
| 6 | Semgrep "basic authentication" (High) on the organizer endpoint | No question: pre-approved (PA-04). If the agent asks anyway, answer: *use pre-approved.md*. |
| 6 | Stryker reports an implausibly low frontend score (about 25 %) or the agent says mutants are not activated | Approve `vitest` and `@vitest/coverage-v8` 4.1.x, the same version for both; `@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` 10.0.0 does not work with Vitest 5. No question if `tech-stack.md` has 4.1.11. |

Anything the agent decides on its own (for example a scanner false positive rated Medium) needs no answer.

## 4. After the run
1. In the **finished session**, before you close it, copy these numbers from the **Usage panel** (the harness's own figures) into the empty cells of the panel table in `03_statistics/usage.md`: *Cost shown*, *API time*, *Session wall time*, *Tokens shown per model* (input, output, cache read, cache write), *Share of usage at over 150k context* and *Plan limits used*. The transcript of a local session does not always contain these numbers, and without them the cost is not cross-checked. If you type `/cost` and it works, the tool reads the numbers from the transcript and you can skip this.
2. Open a **new session in the same folder** and send exactly:

   ```
   Run node 03_statistics/tools/build-report.mjs --run 03_statistics and report what it prints. Do not change anything else.
   ```

   This measures the run, backs up the transcript to `03_statistics/data/`, writes the report and everything else it generates to `03_statistics/results/`, and fills the empty cells of `usage.md`.
3. Add the number of **approval prompts** to `03_statistics/usage.md` (the only cell it cannot fill).
4. Open `03_statistics/results/run-report.html`. At the top, "Quality gate" shows whether the run reached the gate (a run that did not is not comparable; write down which threshold failed). In "Trust in the measurement" the cost difference should say `ok` (it says "not checked" when no panel numbers were entered: fill them in and send the post-run prompt again) and the phase timestamps should come from the clock tool. If not, write down what you see.
5. Commit the statistics: `git add -A`, `git commit -m "statistics <label>"`. `git status` must not list `.env`. Then push the statistics: `git push` (the branch is already connected from step 1.8).
6. Hand in the run folder, or its branch and the commit SHAs from steps 1.7 and 4.5 (both pushed), plus a note on anything unusual (a repeated run, a usage limit, a manual change).

## If something goes wrong
| Problem | What to do |
|---|---|
| `stat.mjs` or `build-report.mjs` fails with "node not found" | Install Node 20 or newer, open a new terminal, send the same prompt again. |
| The report says no transcript was found | Run `py 03_statistics/tools/claude_chat_to_md.py --list`, find the session, put the path of its `.jsonl` in `03_statistics/run-log.json` → `transcript` (a resumed run: every session file in `transcripts`) and run step 4.2 again. |
| `transcript.md` is missing | Python 3 is not installed. Everything else is complete. |
| The run was resumed in a new session | Same folder, same prompt text. List both session files in `transcripts` before step 4.2. |
| The cost check does not say `ok` | Write it down and hand it in; do not fix numbers by hand. |
# Metrics

> Owner: Experiment lead · Read in: every phase and post-run · Agent: read-only

Experiment measurement only. Record observed values; never estimate. An unobservable value stays `null` with a `<field>Reason`.

Goal column: **↓** lower is better, **↑** higher is better, **=** should equal the stated value, **i** information for interpreting other numbers.

## Principles

- **Human waiting is not part of the result.** Agent time is wall time minus every wait for a human. A wait over one hour also lets the 1-hour prompt cache expire, and the call after it writes the whole context again; that rebuild is a cost of the wait, so `usage.costUsdExclWaits` removes it. Compare runs on agent time and `costUsdExclWaits`.
- **Record only what only you can see, and with the clock tool.** The agent records what happened (waits, loops, decisions, deviations, test and quality results). Timestamps come from `tools/stat.mjs`, never from memory or estimates. Everything that can be computed from the transcripts and git is computed after the run by `tools/build-report.mjs`, so the run spends no calls on it.
- **Make runs comparable.** Say what a number covers. Scope, level and tool of coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

## 1. Agent, during the run → `run-log.json`

Phase 0, first action: `node 03_statistics/tools/stat.mjs init`. It creates `run-log.json` from the template, a unique `runId`, the start time and commit, the transcript path and the environment. It prints what it wrote.

| Field | When | How | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runId`, `model`, `effort`, `templateVersion`, `start`, `startCommit`, `transcript`, `environment` | phase 0 | written by `stat.mjs init` from `run-config.md`, git and the host | i |
| `phases[].start`, `phases[].end` | every phase boundary | `stat.mjs phase <n> start` and `stat.mjs phase <n> end`; a start also closes the previous phase, `phase 7 end` also sets `end` and `finalCommit` | ↓ agent time per phase |
| `humanInterventions[]` | every time the agent waits for the human or the human acts, including stops, restarts and installs | `stat.mjs wait start <cause> "<reason>" [decisionId]` when you ask or stop, `stat.mjs wait end` when work resumes. `cause`: `decision`, `environment`, `approval`, `session`, `other` | ↓ count and minutes; every minute here is excluded from agent time |
| `firstTestRun`, `finalTestRun` | first full run before fixes; last full run | edit the file: `passed`, `failed` and `byLevel` (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e` counts) | first: ↓ failed (defects the first run found); final: ↑ passed, `failed` = 0 |
| `acceptanceCriteria` | end of phase 3; changes in phase 4 | `total` criteria, `frozenTests`, `frozenTestChanges[]` as `{decisionId, reason}` | ↑ criteria covered by tests; ↓ frozen-test changes (each one needed a human) |
| `findings` | end of phase 6 | counts by severity, as found | ↓ |
| `openAtEnd` | end of phase 6 | Critical, High and Medium findings still open after triage | = 0 for Critical and High |
| `fixLoops[]` | each verify → fix → re-verify loop | `{loop, findings, category, needsHuman, change, start, end}`. `category`: `test-gap`, `security-config`, `dependency`, `defect`, `process`, `tooling`. `start` is the first fix action, `end` the clean re-check (UTC, `date -u +%FT%TZ`) | ↓ minutes per loop; a loop that repeats across runs belongs in the template |
| `decisions[]` | each decision record | `{id, type, phase, category, start, end}`; `type` `blocking` or `non-blocking`; `category`: `environment`, `dependency`, `security-finding`, `frozen-test`, `requirement`, `other`; `end` = when resolved | ↓ blocking; a category that repeats across runs can be answered in advance |
| `divergences[]` | whenever the run departs from `AGENTS.md`, `working-rules.md`, `phases.md` or the stack | `{phase, ref, divergence}`; includes steps done without the required question, scope reduced, versions replaced | = 0; each one makes the run less comparable |
| `codeMetrics` | phase 5, updated in phase 6 for a changed component | per component: `productionLoc`, `testLoc`, `lineCoverage` and `branchCoverage` as `{unit, nonUnit, all}`, `mutation` as `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`, plus complexity and duplication; scope, level and counting as in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` | ↑ coverage and mutation score (always with scope); = 0 duplication |
| `codeMetrics.gate` | phase 5, updated in phase 6 | the quality gate of `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: `thresholds`, `perComponent` (`lineMet`, `mutationMet`, shortfalls in points), `mutationRounds` and `testsAtFirstMutation` per component, `met` | `met` true; few rounds |

`commits[]` and `commitSummary` are not recorded by the agent: the post-run step reads them from `git log`.

## 2. Post-run session → `run-log.json`, `results/`, `data/`

Started after the run ends, in a new session whose only task is: "Run `node 03_statistics/tools/build-report.mjs --run 03_statistics` and report what it prints. Do not change anything else." Before it, run `/cost` once in the finished session (the plan limits are then captured in the transcript). The script:

1. measures the run from the session transcript(s), the sub-agent transcripts next to them and `git log`, and stores `time`, `usage`, `environment`, `commits`, `commitSummary` in `run-log.json`;
2. copies the transcripts to `03_statistics/data/` (committed with the run, so the measuring can be repeated on any machine; the recorded path is used when it exists, the copy otherwise);
3. writes everything it generates to `03_statistics/results/`: `run-report.html` (every attribute with goal, direction and value), `measurements.json`, `usage-panel.md`, `commits.csv`, `transcript.md` (readable session, needs Python 3);
4. fills the empty cells of the panel table in `usage.md` from the harness's own accounting (the `cost-state` record in the transcript).

Options: `--no-write` leaves `run-log.json` and `usage.md` alone, `--no-md` skips `transcript.md`, `--no-backup` skips `data/`. If `transcript` is missing from `run-log.json`, find the session with `py 03_statistics/tools/claude_chat_to_md.py --list`, put the path of its `.jsonl` in `transcript` (a resumed run lists every session file in `transcripts`) and run the script again. Without any transcript the report still builds from phases and recorded waits; cost, tokens, model and tool time, context and cache rebuilds are then not recorded.

| Field | What it is | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| `time.agentMin` | sum over phases of wall time minus waits (recorded interventions and idle gaps above 10 minutes in the transcript) | ↓ |
| `time.humanWaitMin`, `time.waitsOver60Min`, `time.longWaits[]` | excluded waiting, and each wait over an hour with its cause | ↓; = 0 waits over an hour |
| `time.modelMin`, `time.toolMin` | transcript time spent generating and running tools | ↓; tool time shows what to automate or speed up |
| `time.unrecordedIdleMin` | idle time in the transcript that `humanInterventions` does not cover | = 0 (a recording gap) |
| `time.phaseChecks` | phase boundaries written by `stat.mjs` against typed ones, and implausible timestamps | all via `stat.mjs`, no issues |
| `time.byPhase[]` | wall, wait, agent, model and tool minutes per phase | ↓ in phases 0, 1, 2, 7 (overhead); phases 4 to 6 hold the real work |
| `usage.inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `thinkingTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, `modelCalls` | sums over every model call, each call counted once, sub-agents included | ↓ |
| `usage.toolCalls` | total, errors, per tool name | ↓ calls and errors |
| `usage.costUsd` | tokens × the prices in `usage.md`, per model | ↓ |
| `usage.costUsdExclWaits` | `costUsd` minus the cache rebuilds that followed a wait over an hour | ↓ (the comparison figure) |
| `usage.cacheRebuilds[]` | each cache write above 150k tokens, the wait before it and its extra cost | = none caused by waits |
| `usage.subagents` | sub-agent calls, transcripts found, their cost (inside `costUsd`) | i; a call without a transcript is a measuring gap |
| `usage.panel`, `usage.check` | the harness's own totals (`cost-state`) and the difference to our calculation | difference within 1.5 % |
| `usage.byPhase[]` | calls, tokens, cost and average context per phase | ↓ in late phases, where context is largest |
| `usage.context` | peak and average context tokens per call, share of calls above 150k | ↓ (every call re-reads the whole context) |
| `usage.toolTimeByCategory` | minutes and calls per command class (backend build, mutation, e2e, …) | ↓ for the largest classes |
| `commits[]` | per commit: phase, type, files, changed lines (without logs, lock files, generated folders), concerns touched, size and message checks, minutes since the previous commit (waits removed), model calls and cost since the previous commit | commits small and finished: ≤ 15 files and ≤ 400 lines, one concern, `<type>: <summary> (IDs)` |
| `commitSummary` | counts, median and maximum size, shares over the size guide, mixed, with a correct message, in a burst (within a minute of the previous), cost and minutes between commits, cost per 100 lines | ↓ oversize, mixed and burst; ↑ correct messages |
| `environment` | operator, machine, plan, permission mode (from `run-config.md`), operating system and tool versions (at the start), harness version, entry point, models, effort and permission modes seen (from the transcripts), measuring host | i; needed to explain differences between runs |

## 3. Human → `usage.md`

Prices before the post-run session (one row per model id, shape as in the file). After it only `Approval prompts` is yours; the other cells are filled automatically when empty, and anything you wrote stays. A mismatch between the harness's total and our calculation is reported in the last row.

# Specification > Written in: phase 2 · Source: `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `project/02_design/*`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes Conference registration: an anonymous participant registers as external participant or student through a React form; the Spring Boot backend validates, stores (PostgreSQL + raw JSON copy), confirms by email and notifies organizers; organizers export an Excel workbook. Versions: `tech-stack.md` only. Contracts: `docs/02_contracts/`. ## 1. System context ``` browser ──HTTP──> frontend (nginx: static files, /api proxy) ──HTTP──> backend (Spring Boot, :8080) ├─ JDBC ──> PostgreSQL ├─ file ──> JSON copy volume ├─ SMTP ──> mail server (Mailpit locally) └─ HTTPS ─> Google reCAPTCHA siteverify production: external nginx (TLS, Let's Encrypt) ──> frontend "/" and backend "/api" ``` - S1.1 The frontend calls the backend only under `/api` (AR-01): `GET /api/form-config`, `POST /api/registrations`, `GET /api/export`. Relative URLs; the same origin is served by nginx locally and in production. - S1.2 Actuator health endpoints are under `/actuator/health/**` and are not routed by the reverse proxy; only container health checks use them. ## 2. Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03) Root package `si.konferenca.registration`. Layered by responsibility; dependencies point downwards only: | Package | Responsibility | May depend on (internal) | |---|---|---| | `web` | REST controllers, request/response DTOs, exception handler, request filters (rate limit, body size, HTTPS-only) | `service`, `conference`, `config` | | `security` | Spring Security configuration, organizer user (BCrypt), security headers, CORS | `config` | | `service` | use cases: register, export; business-rule validation | `domain`, `conference`, `infra`, `config` | | `infra` | adapters to the outside: JSON copy store, mail notifier, reCAPTCHA verifiers, Excel writer | `domain`, `conference`, `config` | | `domain` | JPA entities, repository, registration type | — | | `conference` | conference configuration model (options, consents), loader and startup validation | `config` | | `config` | typed `@ConfigurationProperties` and startup guards | — | Justification: one small API with three use cases; a layered split keeps web, business rules, persistence and external adapters separately testable and lets ArchUnit check the direction. ArchUnit rules (phase 3 tests, DoD-04): (a) the table above as a layered architecture; (b) `domain` and `config` depend on no other internal package; (c) no slice cycles over `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` (AR-03); (d) controllers (`@RestController`) live only in `web`; (e) only `domain` declares `@Entity`; (f) `web` never uses `domain` repositories. ## 3. Conference configuration (US-003, AR-04, BR-04, OQ-01, OQ-02) - S3.1 Source: a JSON file whose location is setting `app.conference.config` (env `CONFERENCE_CONFIG`, Spring resource syntax, default `classpath:conference.json` — local and test only per `environments.md`). Contract: `02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`. - S3.2 Content: `options[]` with `id` (stable, `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`), `name`, `category` (`WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL`, `OTHER`), `active` (default `true`), `availableTo` (subset of `EXTERNAL`, `STUDENT`; default both); `consents[]` with `id`, `text`, `mandatory`. - S3.3 Loaded once at startup. The application refuses to start (exception during context start, non-zero exit) when the file is missing or unparsable, an option id is duplicated, a category is unknown, a name is missing or blank, `availableTo` is empty or holds an unknown type, a consent id is duplicated, or a consent text is missing (AC-003-03). - S3.4 Changing the file and restarting changes the offered options; no code change, the participant fields are fixed in code (BR-01, AC-003-02). - S3.5 Shipped configuration (`backend/src/main/resources/conference.json`): at least one active option per category, one option available only to external participants, one inactive option, and the single mandatory consent `privacy` with the wording from OQ-02. ## 4. REST API (contract `02_contracts/openapi.json`) ### 4.1 `GET /api/form-config` (public, AC-003-01, AC-001-08, AC-002-07) Returns `conferenceName`, `recaptcha {siteKey, testMode}`, `consents[] {id, text, mandatory}`, and only **active** `options[] {id, name, category, availableTo[]}` in configuration order. Never returns inactive options or any secret (AR-07: the site key is the only key and comes from configuration). ### 4.2 `POST /api/registrations` (public, US-001, US-002, US-005, US-006, US-007) Request JSON: `type` (`EXTERNAL`|`STUDENT`), `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization` (external), `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId` (student), `optionIds[]`, `consents[]` (ids of consents given), `recaptchaToken`. Processing order: 1. Body larger than `app.limits.max-body-bytes` (default 16384) → 413; malformed JSON → 400 `{message}`. 2. Field validation, all errors collected (SB-01): - `type` missing/unknown → error `type` (no further type-specific checks). - Text fields are trimmed (BR-02); a required field that is missing, empty or whitespace only → error on that field (AC-001-02, AC-002-02). Max lengths: names 100, email 254, organization/institution/programme 200, student ID 50 → error on that field. - `email` must match `^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$` after trimming and must parse as a strict RFC 822 address; no CR/LF (BR-03, AC-001-04, AC-002-03, SR-05). - Fields of the other type that are present and non-blank → error on that field (D-12). - `optionIds`: each id must exist, be active, be available to the type, and appear once; otherwise error `optionIds` (BR-04, SR-04, OQ-01, OQ-04; AC-001-05, AC-002-04). Missing list = no options. - `consents`: each mandatory consent id must be present → error `consents.` (BR-05, AC-001-06, AC-002-05); unknown consent id → error `consents`. - `recaptchaToken` missing/blank → error `recaptchaToken`. 3. If any error: 400 `{message, fieldErrors[{field, message}]}`; nothing stored, nothing sent. 4. reCAPTCHA verification (S7). Rejected or verifier unavailable → 400 with field error `recaptchaToken` (SR-01, AC-001-07, AC-002-06); nothing stored, nothing sent. 5. Persist (S5) — database row and JSON copy in one unit (AR-05). 6. Send participant confirmation and organizer notification (S6); failures are logged with the registration id only and do not change the response (OQ-03, AC-006-03). 7. 201 `{id, type, firstName, lastName, options[{id, name, category}], registeredAt}` (AC-001-01, AC-002-01). Text is stored exactly as trimmed: Unicode (č, š, ž …) is preserved end to end; the database uses UTF-8 and JSON is written as UTF-8 (BR-03, NFR-01, AC-005-04). Line breaks and markup inside names are accepted as data (AC-006-02 presumes such submissions are accepted); they are neutralised on output (S6, S8, frontend renders text only). ### 4.3 `GET /api/export` (organizer, US-008, BR-08) - S4.3.1 HTTPS-only (SR-06, AC-008-04, D-10): when `app.organizer.https-only` (env `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY`, default `true`) is on and the request is not secure (`request.isSecure()`, derived from `X-Forwarded-Proto` of a trusted proxy) and the client address is not loopback → 403 `{message}` before credentials are evaluated; no data. - S4.3.2 HTTP Basic, single user `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`; the password from `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` is BCrypt-hashed at startup and only the hash is kept (SB-03). Missing or wrong credentials → 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic`, body without registration data (AC-008-02). - S4.3.3 Success: 200, `Content-Type: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. See S8. ### 4.4 Errors (SB-07, ES-07) Every error body is `{message}` or `{message, fieldErrors}` with generic text; no stack traces, exception names, SQL or paths. Unexpected errors → 500 `{"message":"The registration could not be processed. Please try again later."}` (AC-005-03, D-11). Rate limited → 429 `{message}`. Unknown routes → 404 / 401 / 403 from the security chain without internals. ## 5. Persistence (US-005, BR-07, AR-05, AR-06, ES-08) - S5.1 Schema only through Flyway (`db/migration/V1__create_registration.sql`, contract `02_contracts/database.sql`). Tables: `registration` (id uuid, type, first_name, last_name, email, organization, study_institution, study_programme, student_id, registered_at timestamptz), `registration_option` (registration_id, option_id, option_name, category, position), `registration_consent` (registration_id, consent_id, consent_text, given_at timestamptz). Hibernate `ddl-auto=validate`. - S5.2 Registration and consent times: one server timestamp (UTC) taken when the request is accepted; each consent's `given_at` equals it (AC-005-01). - S5.3 Write order in one database transaction: insert rows, flush; write the JSON copy (to `/.json.tmp`, then atomic move to `/.json`); commit. A JSON write failure throws and rolls the transaction back (AC-005-03). A commit failure after the file was written deletes the file. The 201 response is produced only after commit (AR-05). - S5.4 JSON copy directory: setting `app.json-copy.dir` (env `JSON_COPY_DIR`, default `./data/json-copies`), created on first write; on a named volume in Docker (NFR-02). Contract: `02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json`. Content: the accepted registration (`id`, `type`, the fields of that type, `options[{id,name,category}]`, `consents[{id,text,givenAt}]`, `registeredAt`), UTF-8, no internal fields (SR-07). ## 6. Email (US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, OQ-03; contract `02_contracts/emails.json`) - S6.1 Sent synchronously after the commit with SMTP connect/read/write timeouts of 5 s; each send is independent; an exception is caught and logged as `Email failed for registration ` (no personal data). - S6.2 Participant confirmation: To = the validated participant address only; From = setting `app.mail.from` (env `MAIL_FROM`); Subject = `Registration confirmed: ` (no user input in any header); body `text/plain; charset=UTF-8` naming the conference, the participant's first and last name and the selected option names (AC-006-01). User input appears only in the plain-text body, so markup stays literal text and line breaks cannot create headers (AC-006-02). - S6.3 Organizer notification: one message per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (comma separated, at least one, validated at startup); Subject `New registration `; plain-text body listing the submitted data; attachment `registration-.json`, `application/json`, whose bytes are the bytes of the stored JSON copy (AC-007-01, AC-007-02). - S6.4 SMTP host, port, TLS (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_STARTTLS`), credentials (`SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, production only) and `CONFERENCE_NAME` come from configuration (ES-01). ## 7. Anti-automation (SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05; contract `02_contracts/recaptcha.json`) - S7.1 Production verifier: `POST` form `secret`, `response` (and `remoteip`) to `app.recaptcha.verify-url` (default `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify`), timeout 5 s; accepted only when the JSON answer has `success: true`. Any other answer, error or timeout = rejected. - S7.2 Test mode (`RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`, default `false`): no network call; exactly the token `test-pass` is accepted, every other token is rejected. The frontend in test mode shows a labelled checkbox instead of the Google widget that produces this token. - S7.3 Startup guard: setting `app.environment` (env `APP_ENVIRONMENT`, default `production`). The application refuses to start when test mode is on and the environment is not `local` or `test`, or when test mode is off and the site key or secret key is empty (SR-02). ## 8. Excel export (US-008, BR-08, SR-07, NFR-01) One sheet `Registrations`; header row then one row per registration ordered by `registered_at`, columns: `Registration ID`, `Type`, `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, `Organization`, `Study institution`, `Study programme`, `Student ID`, `Options` (option names joined by `; `), `Consents` (` ()` joined by `; `), `Registered at` (ISO-8601 UTC). All values are string cells, so text (including leading `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`) is never evaluated as a formula and Unicode is unchanged (AC-008-01, AC-008-03). No other columns or system data (SR-07). ## 9. Cross-cutting security (SB, SR) - S9.1 Rate limiting (SB-06, SR-03): servlet filter before security, per client IP (after trusted-proxy resolution), fixed one-minute windows: `form-config` 60, `registrations` 10, `export` 10 requests (settings `app.limits.*`; tests use higher values). Excess → 429. Failed organizer logins are covered by the export limit. - S9.2 Body size limit (SR-03): S4.2 step 1; Tomcat `max-http-form-post-size` and `max-swallow-size` also bounded. - S9.3 Security headers (SB-10): backend responses carry `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Frontend nginx sends a CSP allowing only self plus Google reCAPTCHA script/frame origins, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`. - S9.4 CORS: disabled unless `APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` is set (local dev server only). - S9.5 CSRF: the API is stateless (no cookies, no session); CSRF protection is disabled for `/api/**`; Basic credentials are never stored by the browser app. - S9.6 Parameterised queries only (JPA/Spring Data), output encoding: React text rendering (no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`), plain-text emails, string cells (SB-05). - S9.7 Logs: registration id and technical events only; no names, emails, tokens or secrets (SB-07, ES-07). Hibernate SQL logging off. - S9.8 Containers run as non-root users (SB-11): backend user `app` (uid 10001); frontend nginx as user `nginx` on port 8080 with temp paths under `/tmp`. - S9.9 Reverse proxy (SR-08, SB-04): the frontend nginx forwards `/api` with `proxy_set_header Host ` (never `$http_host`), sets `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Forwarded-Proto`; the production nginx example in the backend README does the same and terminates TLS. Backend `server.forward-headers-strategy=native`, trusted proxies = private address ranges (Tomcat default, configurable). - S9.10 Dependency, static and secret scanning (SB-08, SB-09): Dependency-Check, npm audit, SpotBugs, PMD, Semgrep, Gitleaks in phase 6. ## 10. Personal data (SB-12 … SB-14) Only the fields of BR-01, the selected options and consents with timestamps are collected (`security-requirements.md` "Personal data"); purpose and retention per OQ-06 — stored until the operator deletes them; release notes instruct deletion of rows and JSON copies within 12 months after the conference. Consent checkboxes are never preselected (BR-05) and the consent wording is stored with the timestamp. ## 11. # Specification > Written in: phase 2 · Source: `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `project/02_design/*`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes Conference registration: an anonymous participant registers as external participant or student through a React form; the Spring Boot backend validates, stores (PostgreSQL + raw JSON copy), confirms by email and notifies organizers; organizers export an Excel workbook. Versions: `tech-stack.md` only. Contracts: `docs/02_contracts/`. ## 1. System context ``` browser ──HTTP──> frontend (nginx: static files, /api proxy) ──HTTP──> backend (Spring Boot, :8080) ├─ JDBC ──> PostgreSQL ├─ file ──> JSON copy volume ├─ SMTP ──> mail server (Mailpit locally) └─ HTTPS ─> Google reCAPTCHA siteverify production: external nginx (TLS, Let's Encrypt) ──> frontend "/" and backend "/api" ``` - S1.1 The frontend calls the backend only under `/api` (AR-01): `GET /api/form-config`, `POST /api/registrations`, `GET /api/export`. Relative URLs; the same origin is served by nginx locally and in production. - S1.2 Actuator health endpoints are under `/actuator/health/**` and are not routed by the reverse proxy; only container health checks use them. ## 2. Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03) Root package `si.konferenca.registration`. Layered by responsibility; dependencies point downwards only: | Package | Responsibility | May depend on (internal) | |---|---|---| | `web` | REST controllers, request/response DTOs, exception handler, request filters (rate limit, body size, HTTPS-only) | `service`, `conference`, `config` | | `security` | Spring Security configuration, organizer user (BCrypt), security headers, CORS | `config` | | `service` | use cases: register, export; business-rule validation | `domain`, `conference`, `infra`, `config` | | `infra` | adapters to the outside: JSON copy store, mail notifier, reCAPTCHA verifiers, Excel writer | `domain`, `conference`, `config` | | `domain` | JPA entities, repository, registration type | — | | `conference` | conference configuration model (options, consents), loader and startup validation | `config` | | `config` | typed `@ConfigurationProperties` and startup guards | — | Justification: one small API with three use cases; a layered split keeps web, business rules, persistence and external adapters separately testable and lets ArchUnit check the direction. ArchUnit rules (phase 3 tests, DoD-04): (a) the table above as a layered architecture; (b) `domain` and `config` depend on no other internal package; (c) no slice cycles over `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` (AR-03); (d) controllers (`@RestController`) live only in `web`; (e) only `domain` declares `@Entity`; (f) `web` never uses `domain` repositories. ## 3. Conference configuration (US-003, AR-04, BR-04, OQ-01, OQ-02) - S3.1 Source: a JSON file whose location is setting `app.conference.config` (env `CONFERENCE_CONFIG`, Spring resource syntax, default `classpath:conference.json` — local and test only per `environments.md`). Contract: `02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`. - S3.2 Content: `options[]` with `id` (stable, `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`), `name`, `category` (`WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL`, `OTHER`), `active` (default `true`), `availableTo` (subset of `EXTERNAL`, `STUDENT`; default both); `consents[]` with `id`, `text`, `mandatory`. - S3.3 Loaded once at startup. The application refuses to start (exception during context start, non-zero exit) when the file is missing or unparsable, an option id is duplicated, a category is unknown, a name is missing or blank, `availableTo` is empty or holds an unknown type, a consent id is duplicated, or a consent text is missing (AC-003-03). - S3.4 Changing the file and restarting changes the offered options; no code change, the participant fields are fixed in code (BR-01, AC-003-02). - S3.5 Shipped configuration (`backend/src/main/resources/conference.json`): at least one active option per category, one option available only to external participants, one inactive option, and the single mandatory consent `privacy` with the wording from OQ-02. ## 4. REST API (contract `02_contracts/openapi.json`) ### 4.1 `GET /api/form-config` (public, AC-003-01, AC-001-08, AC-002-07) Returns `conferenceName`, `recaptcha {siteKey, testMode}`, `consents[] {id, text, mandatory}`, and only **active** `options[] {id, name, category, availableTo[]}` in configuration order. Never returns inactive options or any secret (AR-07: the site key is the only key and comes from configuration). ### 4.2 `POST /api/registrations` (public, US-001, US-002, US-005, US-006, US-007) Request JSON: `type` (`EXTERNAL`|`STUDENT`), `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization` (external), `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId` (student), `optionIds[]`, `consents[]` (ids of consents given), `recaptchaToken`. Processing order: 1. Body larger than `app.limits.max-body-bytes` (default 16384) → 413; malformed JSON → 400 `{message}`. 2. Field validation, all errors collected (SB-01): - `type` missing/unknown → error `type` (no further type-specific checks). - Text fields are trimmed (BR-02); a required field that is missing, empty or whitespace only → error on that field (AC-001-02, AC-002-02). Max lengths: names 100, email 254, organization/institution/programme 200, student ID 50 → error on that field. - `email` must match `^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$` after trimming and must parse as a strict RFC 822 address; no CR/LF (BR-03, AC-001-04, AC-002-03, SR-05). - Fields of the other type that are present and non-blank → error on that field (D-12). - `optionIds`: each id must exist, be active, be available to the type, and appear once; otherwise error `optionIds` (BR-04, SR-04, OQ-01, OQ-04; AC-001-05, AC-002-04). Missing list = no options. - `consents`: each mandatory consent id must be present → error `consents.` (BR-05, AC-001-06, AC-002-05); unknown consent id → error `consents`. - `recaptchaToken` missing/blank → error `recaptchaToken`. 3. If any error: 400 `{message, fieldErrors[{field, message}]}`; nothing stored, nothing sent. 4. reCAPTCHA verification (S7). Rejected or verifier unavailable → 400 with field error `recaptchaToken` (SR-01, AC-001-07, AC-002-06); nothing stored, nothing sent. 5. Persist (S5) — database row and JSON copy in one unit (AR-05). 6. Send participant confirmation and organizer notification (S6); failures are logged with the registration id only and do not change the response (OQ-03, AC-006-03). 7. 201 `{id, type, firstName, lastName, options[{id, name, category}], registeredAt}` (AC-001-01, AC-002-01). Text is stored exactly as trimmed: Unicode (č, š, ž …) is preserved end to end; the database uses UTF-8 and JSON is written as UTF-8 (BR-03, NFR-01, AC-005-04). Line breaks and markup inside names are accepted as data (AC-006-02 presumes such submissions are accepted); they are neutralised on output (S6, S8, frontend renders text only). ### 4.3 `GET /api/export` (organizer, US-008, BR-08) - S4.3.1 HTTPS-only (SR-06, AC-008-04, D-10): when `app.organizer.https-only` (env `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY`, default `true`) is on and the request is not secure (`request.isSecure()`, derived from `X-Forwarded-Proto` of a trusted proxy) and the client address is not loopback → 403 `{message}` before credentials are evaluated; no data. - S4.3.2 HTTP Basic, single user `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`; the password from `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` is BCrypt-hashed at startup and only the hash is kept (SB-03). Missing or wrong credentials → 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic`, body without registration data (AC-008-02). - S4.3.3 Success: 200, `Content-Type: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. See S8. ### 4.4 Errors (SB-07, ES-07) Every error body is `{message}` or `{message, fieldErrors}` with generic text; no stack traces, exception names, SQL or paths. Unexpected errors → 500 `{"message":"The registration could not be processed. Please try again later."}` (AC-005-03, D-11). Rate limited → 429 `{message}`. Unknown routes → 404 / 401 / 403 from the security chain without internals. ## 5. Persistence (US-005, BR-07, AR-05, AR-06, ES-08) - S5.1 Schema only through Flyway (`db/migration/V1__create_registration.sql`, contract `02_contracts/database.sql`). Tables: `registration` (id uuid, type, first_name, last_name, email, organization, study_institution, study_programme, student_id, registered_at timestamptz), `registration_option` (registration_id, option_id, option_name, category, position), `registration_consent` (registration_id, consent_id, consent_text, given_at timestamptz). Hibernate `ddl-auto=validate`. - S5.2 Registration and consent times: one server timestamp (UTC) taken when the request is accepted; each consent's `given_at` equals it (AC-005-01). - S5.3 Write order in one database transaction: insert rows, flush; write the JSON copy (to `/.json.tmp`, then atomic move to `/.json`); commit. A JSON write failure throws and rolls the transaction back (AC-005-03). A commit failure after the file was written deletes the file. The 201 response is produced only after commit (AR-05). - S5.4 JSON copy directory: setting `app.json-copy.dir` (env `JSON_COPY_DIR`, default `./data/json-copies`), created on first write; on a named volume in Docker (NFR-02). Contract: `02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json`. Content: the accepted registration (`id`, `type`, the fields of that type, `options[{id,name,category}]`, `consents[{id,text,givenAt}]`, `registeredAt`), UTF-8, no internal fields (SR-07). ## 6. User input appears only in the plain-text body, so markup stays literal text and line breaks cannot create headers (AC-006-02). - S6.3 Organizer notification: one message per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (comma separated, at least one, validated at startup); Subject `New registration `; plain-text body listing the submitted data; attachment `registration-.json`, `application/json`, whose bytes are the bytes of the stored JSON copy (AC-007-01, AC-007-02). - S6.4 SMTP host, port, TLS (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_STARTTLS`), credentials (`SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, production only) and `CONFERENCE_NAME` come from configuration (ES-01). ## 7. Anti-automation (SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05; contract `02_contracts/recaptcha.json`) - S7.1 Production verifier: `POST` form `secret`, `response` (and `remoteip`) to `app.recaptcha.verify-url` (default `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify`), timeout 5 s; accepted only when the JSON answer has `success: true`. Any other answer, error or timeout = rejected. - S7.2 Test mode (`RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`, default `false`): no network call; exactly the token `test-pass` is accepted, every other token is rejected.
